hints.content:
$h$ is increasing in an interval where as $x$ increases, $h(x)$ also increases.

Visually, this is where the graph is going upwards as we go from left to right.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by ten. The graph of y equals h of x is a continuous curve. From left to right, it passes through the point negative five, twenty-two and it decreases through the x-intercept negative four, zero until the local minimum at negative three, negative eight. Then it increases through the x-intercept negative one, zero until the local maximum at zero, four. then it decreases through the x-intercept one, zero, the point two, negative twenty, and the point three, negative fifty-five. All values are estimated. The function is highlighted from x equals negative three to x equals zero.

hints.content:
Now we can check each option:

Interval | Is $h$ increasing on the interval?
:-: | :-:
$-5<x<-3$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $h$ is decreasing on this interval
$-2<x<0$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
$0<x<2$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $h$ is decreasing on this interval
